newsitem.title: UK: DML partners seal purchase of Devonport naval dock.
newsitem.headline: DML partners seal purchase of Devonport naval dock.

text.p: An Anglo-American consortium of engineering and services companies confirmed on Tuesday that it had agreed terms to buy the Devonport Royal Naval Dockyard in Plymouth from the government for 40.3 million stg.

"The consideration for the yard is approximately 40.3 million stg, which will be paid in cash on completion," cables and engineering company BICC Plc said in a statement issued on behalf of the partners which include Halliburton Co of the United States and Weir Group Plc.

As part of the sale agreement, the Devonport Management Ltd (DML) partnership will continue to provide nuclear refuelling and refitting facilities in support of Trident and other nuclear submarines into the next century, the Ministry of Defence said in a parallel statement.
Some 4,500 people work at the dockyard and consultations with trades unions have been completed.
Late last year, the MoD signed a contract with Babcock International Group Plc for the sale of the other main UK naval service facility, Rosyth Royal Dockyard, which was completed on January 30.
"Both these deals represent good value for money and are good news for the taxpayer," James Arbuthnot, Minister of State for Defence Procurement, said in answer to a parliamentary question.
The DML deal will be completed once the necessary nuclear and other authorisations have been cleared, he said.
The companies said they expected this to be completed in about four weeks' time.
